lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! You're very welcome – I'm happy to help you find out if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Since Alex is 8 years old, that's well within the age range for Child Benefit.

Next, could you tell me where you and Alex live? Specifically, are you both living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. But Alex doesn't live with me, he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation with Alex? Specifically:

- Does Alex's mum already claim Child Benefit for him?
- Do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep at all (for example, by paying maintenance or regularly buying things he needs)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His mum does already claim Child Benefit for Alex, yes. I do help out a bit though - I contribute towards things like his school clothes and bits and pieces he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information – it's really helpful.

Since Alex's mum already claims Child Benefit for him and Alex lives with her, there's an important rule to be aware of: only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time. Generally, the person the child lives with has priority for the claim.

Even though you contribute towards Alex's costs, because he lives with his mum and she is already receiving Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to make a separate claim for Alex.

However, if there were ever a change in circumstances – for example, if Alex came to live with you – you could then make a claim.

Let me confirm this outcome for you now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's a summary of the reasons:

**For Alex:**
- ✗ **Not eligible** – Although Alex is 8 years old and within the qualifying age for Child Benefit, he lives with his mum, not with you. His mum already claims Child Benefit for him. Under UK rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time, and priority is given to the person the child lives with.

**What this means for you:**
Since Alex's mum has priority because Alex lives with her and she's already receiving the benefit, you cannot make a separate claim for him – even though you contribute towards his costs.

If your circumstances ever change (for example, if Alex comes to live with you), you would then be able to apply for Child Benefit.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
